content:
We need to combine subnetworks into full topology. Subnet 1 has resistors R1-R4, subnet2 R1-R3, subnet3 R1-R3. But resistor IDs conflict; need unique IDs across whole network. Also need to ensure connections consistent: Subnet1 ends at X1, subnet2 starts at X1 and ends at X2, subnet3 ends at X2 and starts at B. So overall chain A -> ... -> X1 -> ... -> X2 -> ... -> B. Need to rename resistors to unique IDs, maybe prefix with subnet number: S1_R1 etc.

Also need to include all resistors: total 4+3+3 =10 matches note.

Construct combined topology: resistors dict with 10 entries.

List connections in order:

Subnet1 connections:
["A","N_a1","S1_R1"]
["N_a1","N_a2","S1_R2"]
["N_a2","N_a3","S1_R3"]
["N_a3","X1","S1_R4"]

Subnet2:
["X1","N_b1","S2_R1"]
["N_b1","N_b2","S2_R2"]
["N_b2","X2","S2_R3"]

Subnet3:
["B","N_c2","S3_R1"]
["N_c2","N_c1","S3_R2"]
["N_c1","X2","S3_R3"]

Check resistor values: from given inputs.

Subnet1 values: R1 5, R2 10, R3 15, R4 20.

Subnet2: R1 10, R2 15, R3 20.

Subnet3: R1 20, R2 15, R3 10.

Thus mapping.

Now we should maybe validate against measurements using simulate and validate tools to ensure correct? Could be optional but good to verify. Let's simulate resistance between A and B should be 140 per measurements.

We'll construct topology JSON and call simulate_circuit_resistance.
